knowledge:
- key_parameters: data_files=Vector of file paths (e.g., CSVs) containing the experimental condition datasets ;; data_column=Vector of column names representing the time points/kinetics data matrix ;; nClusters=The number of desired clusters for the clustering algorithm ;; chosen_model=Clustering method to use, either 'mclust' (default, model-based) or 'kmeans' ;; comigration_size=Minimum number of comigrated proteins/features to filter the alluvial plot results ;; ggplot_theme=Custom ggplot2 theme to format the cluster and composition plots
- alternatives: chosen_model='kmeans' can be used as an alternative to the default model-based clustering ('mclust')
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing quantitative time-series omics data (labeled or label-free proteomics, transcriptomics) across multiple experimental conditions to find co-abundance patterns, comigrating features, and functional PPI networks.
- pitfalls: mclust requires setting a fixed random seed (set.seed) to get reproducible clustering results ;; Column names for the kinetics data matrix must be identical across all input datasets ;; If the number of selected conditions is greater than 2, XINA cannot apply the enrichment filter, and pval_threshold is ignored in alluvial_enriched.

workflows.name: xina_time_series_clustering_and_network_analysis
workflows.intent: Cluster multiplexed time-series omics data across multiple conditions, identify comigrated features, and perform PPI network analysis.
input: Control.csv (quantitative time-series data for Control condition)
workflows.stages: 1. Load quantitative time-series datasets for each condition ;; 2. Define the time points (columns) and data files ;; 3. Perform model-based or k-means clustering using xina_clustering ;; 4. Plot the clusters using plot_clusters and condition compositions using plot_condition_compositions ;; 5. Perform coregulation/comigration analysis using alluvial_enriched ;; 6. Perform PPI network analysis using STRINGdb and xina_analysis ;; 7. Plot PPI networks using xina_plot_all
workflows.code:
library(XINA)
random_data_info <- make_random_xina_data()
Control <- read.csv("Control.csv", check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
Stimulus1 <- read.csv("Stimulus1.csv", check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
Stimulus2 <- read.csv("Stimulus2.csv", check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
set.seed(0)
data_files <- paste(random_data_info$conditions, ".csv", sep='')
data_column <- random_data_info$time_points
clustering_result <- xina_clustering(data_files, data_column=data_column, nClusters=20)
clustering_result_km <- xina_clustering(data_files, data_column=data_column, nClusters=20, chosen_model='kmeans')
library(ggplot2)
theme1 <- theme(title=element_text(size=8, face='bold'),
                axis.text.x = element_text(size=7),
                axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
                axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
                axis.title.x = element_blank(),
                axis.title.y = element_blank())
plot_clusters(clustering_result, ggplot_theme=theme1)
theme2 <- theme(legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm"),
                legend.text=element_text(size=5),
                title=element_text(size=7, face='bold'))
condition_composition <- plot_condition_compositions(clustering_result, ggplot_theme=theme2)
classes <- as.vector(clustering_result$condition)
all_cor <- alluvial_enriched(clustering_result, classes)
cor_bigger_than_5 <- alluvial_enriched(clustering_result, classes, comigration_size=5)
library(STRINGdb)
string_db <- STRINGdb$new( version="10", species=9606, score_threshold=0, input_directory="" )
xina_result <- xina_analysis(clustering_result, string_db)
xina_plot_all(xina_result, clustering_result)
